Question 1 of 20, Level 1

1MCQCBSE SQP 2026-271 mark
The degree and order of the differential equation y−x(dydx)3=a(y+d2ydx2)2y-x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3=a\left(y+\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2y−x(dxdy​)3=a(y+dx2d2y​)2 are respectively:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Order = order of the highest derivative; degree = power of that derivative, once the equation is a polynomial in derivatives.

  1. 1

    The highest order derivative is d2ydx2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}dx2d2y​.

    Order=2\text{Order}=2Order=2
  2. 2

    The equation is a polynomial in derivatives. On expanding, d2ydx2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}dx2d2y​ has highest power 222.

    Degree=2\text{Degree}=2Degree=2
    1
  3. 3

    Degree first, then order: 2, 22,\ 22, 2. Hence option (B).

Answer(B) 2, 2\displaystyle 2,\ 22, 2

Watch out Reading the degree as 333 from (dydx)3\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3(dxdy​)3; the degree is the power of the highest order derivative only.

Chapter 9Question 2

Question 2 of 20, Level 1

2MCQNCERT Exemplar Q351 mark
The degree of the differential equation [1+(dydx)2]32=d2ydx2\left[1+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^{\frac{3}{2}}=\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}[1+(dxdy​)2]23​=dx2d2y​ is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Degree is a positive integer; first remove fractional powers of derivatives, then read the power of the highest derivative.

  1. 1

    The power 32\dfrac{3}{2}23​ is not an integer. Square both sides to remove it.

    [1+(dydx)2]3=(d2ydx2)2\left[1+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^{3}=\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2[1+(dxdy​)2]3=(dx2d2y​)2[1+(dydx)2]3=(d2ydx2)2\displaystyle \left[1+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^{3}=\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2[1+(dxdy​)2]3=(dx2d2y​)2
  2. 2

    Now it is a polynomial in derivatives. The highest derivative d2ydx2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}dx2d2y​ has power 222.

    Degree=2\text{Degree}=2Degree=2
    1
  3. 3

    Hence option (D).

Answer(D) 2\displaystyle 22

Watch out Answering 32\dfrac{3}{2}23​ or 'not defined'; a fractional power is removed by squaring, and the degree is then 222.

The integrating factor of the differential equation dydx+y=1+yx\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=\dfrac{1+y}{x}dxdy​+y=x1+y​ is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea For dydx+Py=Q\dfrac{dy}{dx}+Py=Qdxdy​+Py=Q, I.F.=e∫P dx\text{I.F.}=e^{\int P\,dx}I.F.=e∫Pdx.

  1. 1

    Split the right side and bring the yyy term to the left.

    dydx+(1−1x)y=1x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\left(1-\dfrac{1}{x}\right)y=\dfrac{1}{x}dxdy​+(1−x1​)y=x1​dydx+(1−1x)y=1x\displaystyle \dfrac{dy}{dx}+\left(1-\dfrac{1}{x}\right)y=\dfrac{1}{x}dxdy​+(1−x1​)y=x1​
  2. 2

    Compare with dydx+Py=Q\dfrac{dy}{dx}+Py=Qdxdy​+Py=Q and integrate PPP.

    P=1−1x,∫P dx=x−log⁡xP=1-\dfrac{1}{x},\qquad \displaystyle\int P\,dx=x-\log xP=1−x1​,∫Pdx=x−logxP=1−1x,∫P dx=x−log⁡x\displaystyle P=1-\dfrac{1}{x},\qquad \displaystyle\int P\,dx=x-\log xP=1−x1​,∫Pdx=x−logx
  3. 3

    Find the integrating factor.

    I.F.=ex−log⁡x=ex⋅e−log⁡x=exx\text{I.F.}=e^{x-\log x}=e^x\cdot e^{-\log x}=\dfrac{e^x}{x}I.F.=ex−logx=ex⋅e−logx=xex​I.F.=ex−log⁡x=ex⋅e−log⁡x=exx\displaystyle \text{I.F.}=e^{x-\log x}=e^x\cdot e^{-\log x}=\dfrac{e^x}{x}I.F.=ex−logx=ex⋅e−logx=xex​
    1
  4. 4

    Hence option (B).

Answer(B) exx\displaystyle \dfrac{e^x}{x}xex​

Watch out Taking P=1P=1P=1 and choosing exe^xex; the yx\dfrac{y}{x}xy​ hidden in 1+yx\dfrac{1+y}{x}x1+y​ is also part of PPP.

Question 3Question 5

5MCQNCERT Exemplar Q731 mark
The general solution of the differential equation (ex+1) y dy=(y+1) ex dx(e^x+1)\,y\,dy=(y+1)\,e^x\,dx(ex+1)ydy=(y+1)exdx is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Variable separable: put all yyy terms with dydydy and all xxx terms with dxdxdx, then integrate.

  1. 1

    Separate the variables.

    yy+1 dy=exex+1 dx\dfrac{y}{y+1}\,dy=\dfrac{e^x}{e^x+1}\,dxy+1y​dy=ex+1ex​dxyy+1 dy=exex+1 dx\displaystyle \dfrac{y}{y+1}\,dy=\dfrac{e^x}{e^x+1}\,dxy+1y​dy=ex+1ex​dx
  2. 2

    Write yy+1=1−1y+1\dfrac{y}{y+1}=1-\dfrac{1}{y+1}y+1y​=1−y+11​ and integrate both sides.

    y−log⁡∣y+1∣=log⁡(ex+1)+log⁡ky-\log|y+1|=\log\left(e^x+1\right)+\log ky−log∣y+1∣=log(ex+1)+logky−log⁡∣y+1∣=log⁡(ex+1)+log⁡k\displaystyle y-\log|y+1|=\log\left(e^x+1\right)+\log ky−log∣y+1∣=log(ex+1)+logk
    1
  3. 3

    Move log⁡∣y+1∣\log|y+1|log∣y+1∣ to the right and combine the logs.

    y=log⁡{k(y+1)(ex+1)}y=\log\left\{k(y+1)\left(e^x+1\right)\right\}y=log{k(y+1)(ex+1)}y=log⁡{k(y+1)(ex+1)}\displaystyle y=\log\left\{k(y+1)\left(e^x+1\right)\right\}y=log{k(y+1)(ex+1)}
  4. 4

    Hence option (C).

Answer(C) y=log⁡{k(y+1)(ex+1)}\displaystyle y=\log\left\{k(y+1)\left(e^x+1\right)\right\}y=log{k(y+1)(ex+1)}

Watch out Moving −log⁡∣y+1∣-\log|y+1|−log∣y+1∣ across without changing its sign, which gives option (D).

Assertion (A): y=aex+bexy=ae^{x}+be^{x}y=aex+bex, where aaa and bbb are arbitrary constants, is the general solution of the differential equation d2ydx2−2dydx+y=0\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}-2\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=0dx2d2y​−2dxdy​+y=0. Reason (R): The general solution of a differential equation contains as many arbitrary constants as the order of the equation.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

  1. 1

    Combine the terms: a+ba+ba+b is one constant AAA.

    y=(a+b)ex=Aexy=(a+b)e^x=Ae^xy=(a+b)ex=Aex
  2. 2

    Check: y′=y′′=Aexy'=y''=Ae^xy′=y′′=Aex, so yyy satisfies the equation.

    Aex−2Aex+Aex=0Ae^x-2Ae^x+Ae^x=0Aex−2Aex+Aex=0
  3. 3

    It has only one arbitrary constant, but the order is 222. So A is false.

  4. 4

    R is the definition of a general solution. So R is true.

  5. 5

    A is false and R is true. Hence option (D).

    1
Answer(D) A is false, but R is true.

Watch out Counting aaa and bbb as two constants; aex+bex=(a+b)exae^x+be^x=(a+b)e^xaex+bex=(a+b)ex has only one.

Find the general solution of the differential equation dydx+1−y21−x2=0\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\sqrt{\dfrac{1-y^2}{1-x^2}}=0dxdy​+1−x21−y2​​=0.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea ∫dt1−t2=sin⁡−1t+C\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}=\sin^{-1}t+C∫1−t2​dt​=sin−1t+C

  1. 1

    Separate the variables.

    dy1−y2=−dx1−x2\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1-y^2}}=-\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}1−y2​dy​=−1−x2​dx​dy1−y2=−dx1−x2\displaystyle \dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1-y^2}}=-\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}1−y2​dy​=−1−x2​dx​
    ½
  2. 2

    Integrate both sides.

    ∫dy1−y2=−∫dx1−x2 ⇒ sin⁡−1y=−sin⁡−1x+C\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1-y^2}}=-\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\ \Rightarrow\ \sin^{-1}y=-\sin^{-1}x+C∫1−y2​dy​=−∫1−x2​dx​ ⇒ sin−1y=−sin−1x+C∫dy1−y2=−∫dx1−x2 ⇒ sin⁡−1y=−sin⁡−1x+C\displaystyle \displaystyle\int\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1-y^2}}=-\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\ \Rightarrow\ \sin^{-1}y=-\sin^{-1}x+C∫1−y2​dy​=−∫1−x2​dx​ ⇒ sin−1y=−sin−1x+C
    1
  3. 3

    Hence the general solution is sin⁡−1x+sin⁡−1y=C\sin^{-1}x+\sin^{-1}y=Csin−1x+sin−1y=C.

    ½
Answersin⁡−1x+sin⁡−1y=C\displaystyle \sin^{-1}x+\sin^{-1}y=Csin−1x+sin−1y=C

Watch out Losing the minus sign when moving 1−y21−x2\sqrt{\dfrac{1-y^2}{1-x^2}}1−x21−y2​​ to the right side.

The population of a town increases at a rate proportional to the population present at that time, the constant of proportionality being k (k>0)k\ (k>0)k (k>0). Show that the population doubles in time log⁡2k\dfrac{\log 2}{k}klog2​, whatever the initial population.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Rate proportional to amount: dPdt=kP\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kPdtdP​=kP gives P=P0ektP=P_0e^{kt}P=P0​ekt.

  1. 1

    Let PPP be the population at time ttt, and P0P_0P0​ at t=0t=0t=0.

    dPdt=kP\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kPdtdP​=kP
    ½
  2. 2

    Separate and integrate.

    dPP=k dt ⇒ log⁡P=kt+C\dfrac{dP}{P}=k\,dt\ \Rightarrow\ \log P=kt+CPdP​=kdt ⇒ logP=kt+CdPP=k dt ⇒ log⁡P=kt+C\displaystyle \dfrac{dP}{P}=k\,dt\ \Rightarrow\ \log P=kt+CPdP​=kdt ⇒ logP=kt+C
  3. 3

    At t=0t=0t=0, P=P0P=P_0P=P0​, so C=log⁡P0C=\log P_0C=logP0​.

    log⁡PP0=kt ⇒ P=P0ekt\log\dfrac{P}{P_0}=kt\ \Rightarrow\ P=P_0e^{kt}logP0​P​=kt ⇒ P=P0​ektlog⁡PP0=kt ⇒ P=P0ekt\displaystyle \log\dfrac{P}{P_0}=kt\ \Rightarrow\ P=P_0e^{kt}logP0​P​=kt ⇒ P=P0​ekt
    ½
  4. 4

    Let TTT be the doubling time. Put P=2P0P=2P_0P=2P0​.

    2P0=P0ekT ⇒ ekT=22P_0=P_0e^{kT}\ \Rightarrow\ e^{kT}=22P0​=P0​ekT ⇒ ekT=2
    ½
  5. 5

    Take log. P0P_0P0​ has cancelled, so TTT does not depend on the initial population.

    T=log⁡2kT=\dfrac{\log 2}{k}T=klog2​
    ½
AnswerP=P0ekt\displaystyle P=P_0e^{kt}P=P0​ekt; doubling time T=log⁡2k\displaystyle T=\dfrac{\log 2}{k}T=klog2​, which does not involve P0\displaystyle P_0P0​

Watch out Putting P=2P=2P=2 instead of P=2P0P=2P_0P=2P0​; doubling means twice the starting value.

    (x+1)dydx=2−eyey(x+1)\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2-e^y}{e^y}(x+1)dxdy​=ey2−ey​

    Separate the variables.

    ∫ey2−ey dy=−∫dtt=−log⁡∣2−ey∣\displaystyle\int\dfrac{e^y}{2-e^y}\,dy=-\int\dfrac{dt}{t}=-\log|2-e^y|∫2−eyey​dy=−∫tdt​=−log∣2−ey∣∫ey2−ey dy=−∫dtt=−log⁡∣2−ey∣\displaystyle \displaystyle\int\dfrac{e^y}{2-e^y}\,dy=-\int\dfrac{dt}{t}=-\log|2-e^y|∫2−eyey​dy=−∫tdt​=−log∣2−ey∣
    ½
  4. 4

    Integrate both sides.

    −log⁡∣2−ey∣=log⁡∣x+1∣+C-\log|2-e^y|=\log|x+1|+C−log∣2−ey∣=log∣x+1∣+C
    ½
  5. 5

    Put x=0x=0x=0, y=0y=0y=0.

    −log⁡1=log⁡1+C ⇒ C=0-\log 1=\log 1+C\ \Rightarrow\ C=0−log1=log1+C ⇒ C=0
    ½
  6. 6

    So log⁡∣2−ey∣+log⁡∣x+1∣=0\log|2-e^y|+\log|x+1|=0log∣2−ey∣+log∣x+1∣=0. Near (0,0)(0,0)(0,0) both factors are positive.

    (2−ey)(x+1)=1 ⇒ ey=2−1x+1=2x+1x+1(2-e^y)(x+1)=1\ \Rightarrow\ e^y=2-\dfrac{1}{x+1}=\dfrac{2x+1}{x+1}(2−ey)(x+1)=1 ⇒ ey=2−x+11​=x+12x+1​(2−ey)(x+1)=1 ⇒ ey=2−1x+1=2x+1x+1\displaystyle (2-e^y)(x+1)=1\ \Rightarrow\ e^y=2-\dfrac{1}{x+1}=\dfrac{2x+1}{x+1}(2−ey)(x+1)=1 ⇒ ey=2−x+11​=x+12x+1​
    ½
  7. 7

    Take log. Hence the particular solution is y=log⁡∣2x+1x+1∣y=\log\left|\dfrac{2x+1}{x+1}\right|y=log​x+12x+1​​.

    y=log⁡∣2x+1x+1∣y=\log\left|\dfrac{2x+1}{x+1}\right|y=log​x+12x+1​​
    ½
Answery=log⁡∣2x+1x+1∣\displaystyle y=\log\left|\dfrac{2x+1}{x+1}\right|y=log​x+12x+1​​

Solve the differential equation [e−2xx−yx]dxdy=1  (x≠0)\left[\dfrac{e^{-2\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}-\dfrac{y}{\sqrt{x}}\right]\dfrac{dx}{dy}=1\ \ (x\neq 0)[x​e−2x​​−x​y​]dydx​=1  (x=0).

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea For dydx+Py=Q\dfrac{dy}{dx}+Py=Qdxdy​+Py=Q: y⋅I.F.=∫Q⋅I.F. dx+Cy\cdot\text{I.F.}=\displaystyle\int Q\cdot\text{I.F.}\,dx+Cy⋅I.F.=∫Q⋅I.F.dx+C, where I.F.=e∫P dx\text{I.F.}=e^{\int P\,dx}I.F.=e∫Pdx.

  1. 1

    Take the reciprocal to get dydx\dfrac{dy}{dx}dxdy​.

    dydx=e−2xx−yx\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{e^{-2\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}-\dfrac{y}{\sqrt{x}}dxdy​=x​e−2x​​−x​y​dydx=e−2xx−yx\displaystyle \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{e^{-2\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}-\dfrac{y}{\sqrt{x}}dxdy​=x​e−2x​​−x​y​
    ½
  2. 2

    Rearrange: it is linear in yyy.

    dydx+1x y=e−2xx,P=1x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,y=\dfrac{e^{-2\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}},\qquad P=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}dxdy​+x​1​y=x​e−2x​​,P=x​1​dydx+1x y=e−2xx,P=1x\displaystyle \dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,y=\dfrac{e^{-2\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}},\qquad P=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}dxdy​+x​1​y=x​e−2x​​,P=x​1​
    ½
  3. 3

    Find the integrating factor.

    ∫dxx=2x ⇒ I.F.=e2x\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x}}=2\sqrt{x}\ \Rightarrow\ \text{I.F.}=e^{2\sqrt{x}}∫x​dx​=2x​ ⇒ I.F.=e2x​∫dxx=2x ⇒ I.F.=e2x\displaystyle \displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x}}=2\sqrt{x}\ \Rightarrow\ \text{I.F.}=e^{2\sqrt{x}}∫x​dx​=2x​ ⇒ I.F.=e2x​
    ½
  4. 4

    Write the solution formula.

    y e2x=∫e−2xx⋅e2x dx+Cy\,e^{2\sqrt{x}}=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{e^{-2\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\cdot e^{2\sqrt{x}}\,dx+Cye2x​=∫x​e−2x​​⋅e2x​dx+Cy e2x=∫e−2xx⋅e2x dx+C\displaystyle y\,e^{2\sqrt{x}}=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{e^{-2\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\cdot e^{2\sqrt{x}}\,dx+Cye2x​=∫x​e−2x​​⋅e2x​dx+C
    ½
  5. 5

    The exponentials cancel. Integrate.

    y e2x=∫x−12 dx=2x+Cy\,e^{2\sqrt{x}}=\displaystyle\int x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\,dx=2\sqrt{x}+Cye2x​=∫x−21​dx=2x​+Cy e2x=∫x−12 dx=2x+C\displaystyle y\,e^{2\sqrt{x}}=\displaystyle\int x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\,dx=2\sqrt{x}+Cye2x​=∫x−21​dx=2x​+C
    ½
  6. 6

    Hence the general solution is y e2x=2x+Cy\,e^{2\sqrt{x}}=2\sqrt{x}+Cye2x​=2x​+C.

    ½
Answery e2x=2x+C\displaystyle y\,e^{2\sqrt{x}}=2\sqrt{x}+Cye2x​=2x​+C

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Homogeneous equation dydx=g(yx)\dfrac{dy}{dx}=g\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)dxdy​=g(xy​): put y=vxy=vxy=vx, dydx=v+xdvdx\dfrac{dy}{dx}=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}dxdy​=v+xdxdv​.

  1. 1

    Divide by x2x^2x2. The right side is a function of yx\dfrac{y}{x}xy​, so it is homogeneous.

    dydx=1+yx+(yx)2\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1+\dfrac{y}{x}+\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2dxdy​=1+xy​+(xy​)2dydx=1+yx+(yx)2\displaystyle \dfrac{dy}{dx}=1+\dfrac{y}{x}+\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2dxdy​=1+xy​+(xy​)2
    ½
  2. 2

    Put y=vxy=vxy=vx.

    v+xdvdx=1+v+v2v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=1+v+v^2v+xdxdv​=1+v+v2
    ½
  3. 3

    Cancel vvv on both sides.

    xdvdx=1+v2x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=1+v^2xdxdv​=1+v2
    ½

    −x22y2+log⁡∣y∣−log⁡∣x∣=−log⁡∣x∣+C ⇒ log⁡∣y∣−x22y2=C-\dfrac{x^2}{2y^2}+\log|y|-\log|x|=-\log|x|+C\ \Rightarrow\ \log|y|-\dfrac{x^2}{2y^2}=C−2y2x2​+log∣y∣−log∣x∣=−log∣x∣+C ⇒ log∣y∣−2y2x2​=C−x22y2+log⁡∣y∣−log⁡∣x∣=−log⁡∣x∣+C ⇒ log⁡∣y∣−x22y2=C\displaystyle -\dfrac{x^2}{2y^2}+\log|y|-\log|x|=-\log|x|+C\ \Rightarrow\ \log|y|-\dfrac{x^2}{2y^2}=C−2y2x2​+log∣y∣−log∣x∣=−log∣x∣+C ⇒ log∣y∣−2y2x2​=C

Formula / idea For dydx+Py=Q\dfrac{dy}{dx}+Py=Qdxdy​+Py=Q: y⋅I.F.=∫Q⋅I.F. dx+Cy\cdot\text{I.F.}=\displaystyle\int Q\cdot\text{I.F.}\,dx+Cy⋅I.F.=∫Q⋅I.F.dx+C, where I.F.=e∫P dx\text{I.F.}=e^{\int P\,dx}I.F.=e∫Pdx.

  1. 1

    Expand ddx(xy)=xdydx+y\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy)=x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+ydxd​(xy)=xdxdy​+y.

    y+xdydx+y=x(sin⁡x+x) ⇒ xdydx+2y=x(sin⁡x+x)y+x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=x(\sin x+x)\ \Rightarrow\ x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2y=x(\sin x+x)y+xdxdy​+y=x(sinx+x) ⇒ xdxdy​+2y=x(sinx+x)y+xdydx+y=x(sin⁡x+x) ⇒ xdydx+2y=x(sin⁡x+x)\displaystyle y+x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=x(\sin x+x)\ \Rightarrow\ x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2y=x(\sin x+x)y+xdxdy​+y=x(sinx+x) ⇒ xdxdy​+2y=x(sinx+x)

    dydx+2x y=sin⁡x+x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{2}{x}\,y=\sin x+xdxdy​+x2​y=sinx+xdydx+2x y=sin⁡x+x\displaystyle \dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{2}{x}\,y=\sin x+xdxdy​+x2​y=sinx+x

Case Study: After a medicine is injected, the body removes it from the blood at a rate proportional to the amount present at that time. A patient is given a dose of 400 mg. After 3 hours, 300 mg of the medicine is still present. Let AAA mg be the amount present ttt hours after the dose.
  1. (i)Write the differential equation satisfied by AAA and state its order and degree.1 mark
  2. (ii)Show that A=400(34)t/3A=400\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{t/3}A=400(43​)t/3.1 mark
  3. (iii)(a)Find the amount of medicine present 6 hours after the dose, and the percentage of the dose removed by then.2 marks
  4. OR
  5. (iii)(b)The next dose is given when the amount falls to 168.75 mg. After how many hours is the next dose given?2 marks

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Rate proportional to amount: dAdt=−kA\dfrac{dA}{dt}=-kAdtdA​=−kA gives A=A0e−ktA=A_0e^{-kt}A=A0​e−kt.

    ½

    ½
Answer (i)dAdt=−kA\displaystyle \dfrac{dA}{dt}=-kAdtdA​=−kA; order 1, degree 1

(ii)1 mark
